source_documents.title: Tuning the dual emission of keto/enol forms of excited-state intramolecular proton transfer (ESIPT) emitters via intramolecular charge transfer (ICT)

reference_evidence_units.quote: The emission spectrum of 6a in toluene exhibits a single emission band around 418 nm with a shoulder peak at 430 nm
reference_evidence_units.subject: 6a
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Toluene, Figure 1 and comparison with O-methyl compound 5a.
reference_evidence_units.statement: 6a has the stated single-band emission, assigned by the authors to the enol form.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: The methoxy control supports an assignment; it does not directly observe proton-transfer dynamics.

reference_evidence_units.quote: there is a large energy difference between S1(enol) and the transition state of ESIPT
reference_evidence_units.subject: 6a
reference_evidence_units.statement: The source finds a high forward proton-transfer barrier and uses it to explain enol-only emission.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Do not label efficient operating ESIPT merely because this molecule has an ESIPT-capable skeleton.

reference_evidence_units.quote: The large solvatochromic shift indicates that the enol-form emissions of 6a and 6c are of typical ICT characters
reference_evidence_units.subject: 6a and 6c
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Solvent-dependent enol emission and Lippert-Mataga analysis.
reference_evidence_units.statement: The source supports CT character in the enol emission.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: This is state-specific; it does not establish ICT for every keto/enol configuration.

reference_evidence_units.quote: Hence, both 6a and 6c do not possess thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TADF) characteristics
reference_evidence_units.subject: 6a and 6c
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Temperature-dependent doped-film and degassed-toluene PL, SI Figures S24/S26 reported in main text.
reference_evidence_units.statement: The authors reject TADF because no long-lived emission or clear oxygen quenching is observed.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Missing SI traces remain unverified. This excludes TADF, not all possible triplet involvement.

reference_evidence_units.quote: the reverse intersystem crossing (RISC) process from T6 (enol) to S1(enol)
reference_evidence_units.subject: 6a
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Calculated high-lying triplet/singlet energies, Figure 7a; device exciton-utilization discussion.
reference_evidence_units.statement: The authors propose high-state RISC as an explanation of exciton utilization.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Near-degenerate computed energies suggest feasibility, not a measured RISC rate or direct observation.

reference_mechanisms.label: ICT_TICT_CT
reference_mechanisms.rationale: Enol stabilization and HLCT emission are central to the target's interpretation.

reference_mechanisms.label: TRIPLET_METAL_ENERGY_TRANSFER
reference_mechanisms.rationale: Retain the explicitly tentative high-state RISC proposal, while excluding TADF. This is a source-supported hypothesis, not confirmed dynamics.
